propositions: A new glob-triggered advisory code-review overlay 'surface-parity' must be added to flag when a write-op's parameter, guard, or required-field surface changes on one adapter (lib, CLI, MCP) without sibling adapters being updated in lockstep.

The overlay fires on diffs touching the three write-surface files (_lib_writes.py, _commands/*, _mcp_writes.py) and remains inert on unrelated changes, catching escaped-bug cases where a guard or arg is added to one entry point and not mirrored.

The overlay is advisory-first (blocking_enabled=false, block_threshold=0.95) and must be wired into both the round_a and round_b batches of the code-review gate so the finder is actually dispatched, mirroring the deletion-impact workflow pattern.

The reviewer prompt must carry false-positive guards (deliberate justified divergence, adapter-bound non-caller-visible params like _creation_channel and return_alias, internal-only refactors) so a compliant lockstep change or justified divergence returns no finding.

The overlay registration (OVERLAY_IDS, criteria_routing.json entry, base-reviewer catalog bullet) must stay in lockstep and pass the existing drift test (test_base_prompt_enumerates_exactly_the_overlay_ids); reviewers/index.json remains unchanged (overlays excluded from selection catalog).

Unit tests must assert overlay membership, routing shape, glob firing on each write adapter, round_a/round_b dispatch, and that threshold_for(["surface-parity"]) resolves to (0.95, False) confirming the advisory non-blocking posture.
